name: Roger Dingledine
contribution: Original Tor developer and long-running coordinator of a decentralised anonymity network.
whyIncluded: Tor is a structural tool: it gives users, journalists and dissidents private access to an uncensored web rather than merely arguing for it.
caveat: Ranking reflects documented infrastructure and public-interest impact, not endorsement of every statement or project decision.

name: Moxie Marlinspike
contribution: Created and led the development of Signal and the Signal Protocol, bringing strong end-to-end encryption to mass-market communications.
whyIncluded: Signal converted privacy from a specialist demand into widely usable infrastructure adopted far beyond one app.
caveat: Ranking concerns privacy infrastructure and adoption, not endorsement of every technical or governance decision.

name: Brewster Kahle
contribution: Founded the Internet Archive and built long-term infrastructure for preserving websites, books, software, audio and public memory.
whyIncluded: An independent archive limits the power of deletion, link rot and institutional forgetting.
caveat: Inclusion recognises preservation and access work; it does not decide every copyright or lending dispute involving the Archive.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
contribution: Invented the World Wide Web and later initiated Solid to return data control and interoperability to users.
whyIncluded: Solid directly addresses platform silos by separating personal data from the applications that use it.
caveat: Ranking concerns open-web architecture and user data control, not endorsement of every implementation or commercial partner.

name: Nick Mathewson
contribution: One of Tor's three original designers and a long-running architect of its anonymity and anti-censorship systems.
whyIncluded: Tor's durability depends on sustained engineering, not only the original concept.
caveat: Ranking reflects documented technical contribution, not endorsement of every network policy or design trade-off.

name: Paul Syverson
contribution: Co-invented onion routing and became one of the three original designers of Tor.
whyIncluded: Onion routing is foundational infrastructure for anonymous and censorship-resistant communication.
caveat: Ranking concerns technical invention and public-interest use, not a claim that anonymity tools are risk-free or always used lawfully.

name: Matthew Hodgson
contribution: Co-founded Matrix, an open protocol for interoperable, decentralised real-time communication.
whyIncluded: Matrix attacks communication silos at the protocol layer by allowing independently operated servers to federate.
caveat: Ranking concerns open protocol design and adoption, not endorsement of every company or deployment using Matrix.

name: Juan Benet
contribution: Created IPFS and founded Protocol Labs to develop infrastructure for open, distributed networks.
whyIncluded: IPFS reduces reliance on location-based centralised hosting by addressing information through content and peer-to-peer distribution.
caveat: Ranking recognises open-network infrastructure; it does not endorse every token, investment or project in the wider ecosystem.

name: Amandine Le Pape
contribution: Co-founded Matrix and has led the organisational work required to sustain its open, federated communications ecosystem.
whyIncluded: Decentralised protocols survive only when governance, adoption and operational structures are built alongside code.
caveat: Ranking concerns documented Matrix stewardship and does not endorse every deployment or business relationship.

name: Eugen Rochko
contribution: Created Mastodon as free, open-source social media that is not owned or controlled by one central authority.
whyIncluded: Mastodon provides a working alternative to platform monopoly through federation and community governance.
caveat: Ranking concerns decentralised social infrastructure, not endorsement of every server policy or community decision.

name: Vitalik Buterin
contribution: Conceived Ethereum and remains a major technical and philosophical contributor to its decentralised protocol ecosystem.
whyIncluded: Ethereum expanded decentralised networks from payments toward general-purpose applications and open governance experiments.
caveat: Ranking recognises protocol contribution; it is not investment advice or endorsement of every application built on Ethereum.

name: Ian Clarke
contribution: Created Freenet, an early peer-to-peer platform designed for decentralised and censorship-resistant communication and publishing.
whyIncluded: Freenet is a foundational attempt to make information availability independent of a central host.
caveat: Ranking concerns infrastructure and research contribution, not a claim that every network use is benign.

name: Bram Cohen
contribution: Invented the BitTorrent protocol, enabling large-scale distribution through user-contributed peer-to-peer infrastructure.
whyIncluded: BitTorrent demonstrated that internet-scale distribution could work without a single central server carrying the full load.
caveat: Ranking recognises protocol impact; it does not endorse copyright infringement or every later corporate use of BitTorrent.
